history.summary: The Nagnechi Mata temple is one of the two famous shrines (with Jogmaya Devi Mandir) atop Barmer Fort (Barmer Garh), built by ruler Rawat Bhima in 1552 AD on a ~1,383-ft hillock on Barmer's outskirts. It hosts a popular Navratri fair. COORDINATE FLAG: geocoded to the Barmer Fort complex (25.74132, 71.38605) - the exact spot of the Garh Mandir within the fort is not separately published (verify). NOTE: do not confuse with the older, more famous Nagnechi shrine at Nagana Dham (Rao Dhuhad, Rathore kuldevi) - a different temple.

name: Nagnechi Mata Temple, Barmer Fort
town_description: Barmer is a historic Thar Desert city in western Rajasthan, known for wood carving, block printing, carpets and folk music. Barmer Fort (Barmer Garh), built in 1552 by Rawat Bhima on a 1,383-ft hillock at the city's edge, anchors the old town; Juna (old Barmer) lies about 25 km away.

travel.road: Fort on a hillock on Barmer's outskirts; reachable by road from the city, then a climb on foot (verify).
